summary: Oracle's headed local browser could reach Google sign-in but Playwright-owned Chromium process launch triggered Google's unsupported-browser rejection. The repair keeps the same local profile and user-visible browser while preferring an installed native Chromium process attached over a validated loopback DevTools endpoint, with bounded startup retries and bundled Chromium fallback. Canonical authentication pages become human-only surfaces: Oracle forces observe/human control and suppresses agent interaction, screenshots, and evidence capture there without stealth, user-agent spoofing, cookie copying, or a second login browser.
learning_objectives: When automation-owned process launch breaks a service compatibility or trust boundary, evaluate whether a user/runtime-owned native process can remain authoritative while automation attaches through a bounded local control channel.
Treat sensitive authentication surfaces as an authority transition: revoke agent interaction and evidence capture and require visible human control rather than relying only on field-level redaction.
Native-process attachment must validate the local endpoint identity, bound retries and cleanup failed processes while keeping fallback runtime semantics explicit.
